patch.description:
Certain updates on Entity trigger KYC re-screening, requiring an updated kyc_details.result and kyc_details.screened_at.

For individual entities, KYC re-screening is triggered by changes to: first name, last name, date of birth, tax ID value, switching between `us_entity` and `non_us_entity` when that adds or removes a tax ID, and an existing identification document (for non-US entities). The requirement applies only when kyc_details has previously been submitted for the entity, and the new kyc_details.screened_at must be later than the previous one.

For business and sole proprietorship entities, KYC re-screening is triggered by changes to: business name, business type, tax ID (US entities), and existing identification document (non-US entities).

Note: Business and sole proprietors cannot switch between US and non-US entities. A new entity must be created in such case.

WireReturnRequestStatus.description:
Current status of the return request.

- For incoming return requests: `response_needed`, `accepted`, `rejected`.
- For outgoing return requests: `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`.

`accepted` and `rejected` are terminal.

WireReturnRequestReason.description:
Reason for the return request.

- `creditor_account_number_invalid` — ISO `AC03`. Wire was sent to the wrong account number.
- `wrong_amount` — ISO `AM09`. Wire amount is not the agreed amount or expected.
- `customer_requested` — ISO `CUST`. The partner's end customer requested the return.
- `duplication` — ISO `DUPL`. Duplicate wire sent.
- `fraud_suspected` — ISO `FRAD`. Fraud suspected.
- `narrative` — ISO `NARR`. Catch-all when no structured reason fits; details field carries the explanation.
- `technical_problem` — ISO `TECH`. A technical issue caused the wire to be sent.
- `undue_payment` — ISO `UPAY`. Payment was not due or for services not performed.
- `per_agent_request` — ISO `AGNT`. Incoming only — Lead is the agent for outgoing payments.
- `other` — Incoming only. Catch-all for unmapped ISO codes received from the counterparty.

WireReturnRequestResolvedBy.description:
The party that resolved the return request.

- `lead` — Resolved by Lead through validation or manual review.
- `client` — Resolved by the partner via API or by initiating a return.
- `counterparty` — Resolved by the counterparty financial institution's response. Outgoing return requests only.

WireReturnRequestRejectionReason.description:
Reason the return request was rejected.

- `account_closed` — ISO `AC04`.
- `non_sufficient_funds` — ISO `AM04`.
- `customer_requested` — ISO `CUST`. Customer declined the return.
- `legal_decision` — ISO `LEGL`.
- `customer_no_response` — ISO `NOAS`. Customer did not respond by the deadline.
- `returned_previously` — ISO `ARDT`. Wire already fully returned. Auto-set by Lead when applicable.
- `narrative` — ISO `NARR`. Catch-all; details field carries the explanation.
- `per_agent_request` — ISO `AGNT`. Incoming only.
- `other` — Incoming only. Catch-all for unmapped ISO codes received from the counterparty.

IntendedRolesEnum.description:
The entity's intended role. Lead highly recommends using this field to confirm data requirements for different roles to minimize errors later. In the event more than 1 role is passed in and at least 1 role doesn’t pass validation, the request will not succeed. It will be an all or nothing behavior.
Lead currently supports:
* `authorized_user`: Individual entity with restricted access to the account, without legal responsibility. Only applies to individual entity.
* `authorized_signer`: Individual entity allowed to sign on behalf of the account holder, without legal responsibility. Only applies to individual entity.
* `account_holder`: Entity with full control and legal responsibility for the account. Applies to all entity types.
* `minor_account_holder`: Individual entity aged 16-17 with account-holder eligibility. Individual entities only.

Addresses using `localhost`, IP literals (e.g., user@[127.0.0.1]), or quoted local parts (e.g., "user"@example.com) are not accepted. Only common, real-world email formats are supported.

line_1.description:
Address line 1 is the required primary street-address field. It must contain the full base address needed to identify the physical location, such as the street number and street name together, or the closest local equivalent in countries where addresses do not use that exact structure.

Use address line 1 for all core location details that describe the main property or thoroughfare. Regardless of how each component of an address is collected from your end-users, they must be combined into address line 1 before sending to Lead.

Do not:
- split the primary street address across line 1 and line 2
- put only the street number in line 1 and the street name in line 2
- pad line 1 with false or altered data just to satisfy validation

line_2.description:
Address line 2 is optional and should be used only for secondary or sub-premise information, such as:
- apartment
- unit
- suite
- floor
- building
- care-of / attention

If there is no secondary or sub-premise information, address line 2 should be blank.

Do not use address line 2 for any part of the primary street address.

- For `individual` entity, possible types are: `drivers_license`, `state_or_provincial_id`, `passport`, `permanent_residency_id`, `military_id`, `national_id`, `matriculate_id`, `other`. Note that `national_id` and `matriculate_id` are not applicable for `us_entity`.

- split the primary street address across line 1 and line 2
- put only the street number in line 1 and the street name in line 2
- pad line 1 with false or altered data just to satisfy validation

Do not use address line 2 for any part of the primary street address.

IntendedEligibilityV2.description:
The relationship types you intend this entity to hold. When you send it, Lead checks the entity's data against every listed type and rejects the request with `422 parameters_invalid` if any fails. The check is all or nothing, and the error returns every failing check, not just the first. Listing fewer types than the entity qualifies for still succeeds, and `eligibility` shows everything it qualifies for.

If the check passes, Lead saves the list and returns it on the entity. On a `PATCH`, Lead checks the entity as it would be after the update, against the list you send or, if you leave the field out, the saved list. Send an empty array to clear the saved list; no check runs.

- Screening and risk: `check_kyc_status`, `check_ofac`, `check_risk_score`, `check_manual_review_status` (a manual review of the entity is pending).
- Relationship type: `check_individual_entity` (only individuals can hold `minor_account_holder`, `authorized_signer`, and `authorized_user`), `check_minor_account_holder_enabled` (your program is not approved for minor account holders).
- Stored data: `invalid_entity` (the entity's stored data fails Lead's current validations, which can happen to an older entity when rules change).

The status of the receivable sale.

- `created`: the sale has been created and its member receivables and amounts are frozen.
- `settled`: the `purchase_amount` has been debited from your account. `core_transaction_id` and `settled_at` are set.
- `failed`: the sale could not be settled because your account has insufficient funds or is closed. `failure` describes why. Any other problem leaves the sale `created`.

The components that make up the sale's `purchase_amount`, in minor units. The components always sum to `purchase_amount`.

This object is an open map: Lead may add new components (for example, a premium) in the future without a version change. Each component is a signed integer, so a component that reduces the amount due is negative. Sum every key present rather than only the ones listed here.

expected_payment_frequency.description:
The expected frequency with which customer payments will occur.

**Calendar-based frequencies:**
- `weekly` — Once per week.
- `biweekly` — Once every two weeks (26 payments/year).
- `semi_monthly` — Twice per month on fixed calendar days (24 payments/year).
- `monthly` — Once per calendar month.
- `quarterly` — Once every calendar quarter (4 payments/year).
- `semi_annually` — Once every 6 months (2 payments/year).
- `annually` — Once per calendar year.
- `business_daily` — Once per business day.

**Fixed-interval frequencies:**
- `fixed_interval` — Payments occur after a fixed number of elapsed days rather than on calendar-based dates. When using this value, `expected_payment_frequency_interval_days` is required.

**Non-time-based frequencies:**
- `maturity` — A single payment at loan maturity.
- `variable` — Repayment does not follow a predictable time-based cadence; instead, payments are event-driven (e.g., repayment occurs the next time funds enter the borrower's account).

or DBA. If the names do not match, the payment is rejected with
`rejection_reason: "name_mismatch"`. On
other rails the creditor name is not matched against the account.

`creditor.payment_rail` is not a blockchain network (`solana`, `base`,
`ethereum`). When `creditor.payment_rail` is `swift`, `address` is also
required.

assigned country code (unassigned or grouping codes such as `EU`/`ZZ`

The currency code for the instructed amount. The debtor is always a fiat
account, so `USD` is the only accepted value.

BlockchainPaymentSettlementCurrencyCode.description:
The currency code for the settlement amount. The value must match the
currency the `creditor.payment_rail` settles in, otherwise the payment is
rejected at creation:

| Rail | Settlement currency |
| --- | --- |
| `ach`, `wire`, `swift` | `USD` |
| `sepa` | `EUR` |
| `spei` | `MXN` |
| `pix` | `BRL` |
| `faster_payments` | `GBP` |
| `bre_b`, `co_bank_transfer` | `COP` |

`USDB` is additionally not available when the creditor or creditor agent is
located in an EEA country.

BlockchainPaymentStatusReasonCode.description:
Machine-readable code explaining why a blockchain payment was rejected.
Present only when `status` is `rejected`.

Closed enum; new values may be added as non-breaking changes, so
integrations should tolerate unknown values. Each value is either
**terminal** (resubmitting the same payment cannot succeed) or **retryable**
(the same payment may be resubmitted once the transient condition clears):

- `payment_could_not_be_processed` — **terminal**. Generic reason used when
  no more specific customer-safe code applies.
- `name_mismatch` — **terminal**. The creditor name did not match the legal
  name on the validated receiving account. Correct the creditor name before
  resubmitting.
- `name_not_validated` — **retryable**. The receiving account's name was not
  validated in time. Resubmit the same payment; it reuses the held account
  and succeeds once validation completes.
- `account_closed` — **terminal**. The receiving account is closed and a
  resubmit cannot succeed.
- `account_number_incorrect` — **terminal**. The receiving account number
  is incorrect.

BlockchainPaymentReturn.description:
Details of the return of a Blockchain Payment, set when funds are sent back rather than
delivered to the creditor. Absent for payments that were never returned.

code.description:
Machine-readable code for why the payment was returned.

Closed set; new values may be added as non-breaking changes, so
integrations should tolerate unknown values. Every value is
**terminal** — the returned payment settles at `posted` with the funds
back in the debtor account, and resubmitting the same payment
unchanged returns it again:

- `account_closed` — The receiving account is closed. Correct the
  creditor details before you send the payment again.
- `account_number_incorrect` — The destination account number is
  incorrect.
- `payment_returned` — The receiving institution returned the payment
  for a reason with no more specific customer-safe code. Contact the
  creditor to confirm the account details before you send the payment
  again.

reason.description:
Human-readable description of the return, paired one-to-one with
`code`. Read `code` to make integration decisions and use `reason` for
display.
reason.example: The destination account has been closed.

CreateBlockchainPaymentRequest.title: CreateBlockchainPaymentRequest
CreateBlockchainPaymentRequest.description:
Creates a payment to a fiat or cross-border creditor.

The blockchain creditor rails (`solana`, `base`, `ethereum`) are advertised
in the `payment_rail` enum but rejected at creation; only fiat and
cross-border creditor rails are currently accepted.

The debtor's available balance is checked at creation: insufficient funds
are normally rejected synchronously with HTTP `400` and no payment is
created. When the balance service is temporarily unavailable the check is
deferred to asynchronous processing, so a successful create response is not
an absolute guarantee of settlement.

reference.description:
An optional reference message for the transfer, passed on to the
recipient on rails that carry a reference.

Formatting requirements depend on `creditor.payment_rail`. The reference
is stored and delivered exactly as submitted — it is never shortened,
stripped, or otherwise altered. A reference that does not meet its
rail's requirements is rejected when the payment is created, with HTTP
`422` and an `invalid_parameters` entry for `reference`.

| `payment_rail` | Length | Allowed characters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ach` | 1–10 | letters, digits, spaces |
| `wire` | 1–140 | any character (line-formatted, see below) |
| `sepa` | 6–140 | letters, digits, spaces, and `& - . /` |
| `spei` | 1–40 | letters, digits, spaces |
| `swift` | 1–190 | letters, digits, spaces, and `/ - ? : ( ) . , ' +` (line-formatted, see below) |
| `pix` | 1–100 | letters, digits, spaces |
| `faster_payments` | 1–18 | letters, digits, spaces |

Additional rules:

- **`wire` and `swift`** references are formatted into at most 4 lines of
  35 characters. Words are kept whole and wrapped at spaces; include your
  own line breaks (`\n`) to control the layout. A single word longer than
  35 characters, or text that cannot fit within 4 lines, is rejected.
- **`sepa`** requires a minimum of 6 characters. If you omit the
  reference on a `sepa` payment, one is generated for you and returned
  on the created payment object.
- **`bre_b`, `co_bank_transfer`, `ethereum`, `base`, and `solana`** do not
  carry a reference; supplying one is rejected.
- Omitting the field, or sending an empty string, is allowed on every
  rail except `sepa` and results in no reference being sent.

- `card_network_settlement`: the receivable was created from a card network settlement. `card_network_settlement_details` is present.

- `investment`: the receivable is held for investment on Lead's balance sheet. A receivable can move from `investment` to `sale`.

interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate applied, as a decimal percent (for example, `9.99` means 9.99%). This is a rate, not an amount. Null when the receivable's source carries no rate, as with card network settlements.

fees.description: The fee amount, in minor units. `0` when the receivable's source carries no fees.

ReceivableSaleDetails.description: The sale this receivable is part of. Each field is set at a different point in the receivable's lifecycle, so either may be null.

receivable_sale_id.description: ID of the receivable sale this receivable belongs to. Null until the sale is created.

request_date.description: The business day the receivable is requested for sale. Once the receivable is grouped into a sale, this is the sale's `request_date`. Null until it is set.

settlement_reporting_id.description: The program's per-network reporting ID for the settlement.

user_credit_balance_id.description: ID of the User Credit Balance the receivable is drawn from.

user_credit_transaction_id.description: ID of the User Credit Transaction that drew on the User Credit Balance and created the receivable.

origination_date.description: The date the receivable originated. For a card network settlement this is the settlement date; for other sources it is the date the source object was created. When receivable data arrives late, this is the date the receivable should have originated on, while `created_at` is when the Receivable object was created. Omitted when the receivable is held for investment.

amount.description:
The overall amount of the receivable, in minor units. Equal to the sum of `amount_breakdown.principal`, `amount_breakdown.interest`, and `amount_breakdown.fees`.

- For receivables held for sale, the amount is locked at the loan amount to be sold when the receivable is reclassified for sale.
- For receivables held for investment, the amount is live: it grows with originations and decreases with payments and charge-offs.

updated_at.description: The ISO-8601 timestamp at which any field on the Receivable object was last updated.
